title: Great Leaders Build Great Teams Daily (thebusinessleaderdaily.substack.com), September 1, 2026
author: The Business Leader Daily
source: The Business Leader Daily (thebusinessleaderdaily.substack.com), The Business Leader
summary: This Business Leader Daily issue argues that a leader's real leverage comes not from personal ability but from how well they assemble, inspire, and develop the people around them. It frames team leadership as a continuous, never-finished discipline spanning role definition, recruiting, alignment on shared goals, and removing obstacles, and urges leaders to periodically reassess whether their current team structure still fits the challenges ahead rather than assuming past success guarantees future fit. The piece closes with a curated set of quotes from Keith Ferrazzi, Adam Bryant and Kevin Sharer, Scott Keller, and Paula Davis that reinforce its central claims: that great teams outperform through mutual accountability rather than leader-centric control, that leaders must hold a firm, uncompromising bar for talent, and that alignment, trust, and a sense of renewal are the three consistent hallmarks of peak team experiences.
points: Frames a leader's core leverage as the ability to assemble, inspire, and develop a team rather than personal individual ability.
Positions team leadership as a continuous discipline -- defining roles, recruiting, aligning goals, and removing obstacles -- not a one-time setup task.
Uses Keith Ferrazzi's distinction between 'leadership' and 'teamship' to argue peer-to-peer feedback and accountability outperform leader-centric control.
Cites Scott Keller's research identifying three consistent dimensions of peak team experience: alignment on direction, high-quality interaction, and a strong sense of renewal.
Urges leaders to periodically reassess whether their current team structure still fits where the business is headed, rather than assuming a team that worked before will keep working.
quotes: A great business story begins with a team, not a product or strategy, but a group of people whose efforts deliver results. As a leader, your leverage comes not from your own abilities but from how effectively you assemble, inspire, and raise those around you.
Think of yourself as an architect, designing the framework that supports your organization's long-term ambitions. Continually assess whether your current team structure fits where your business is.
A good leader gives feedback. A great leader assures the team gives each other feedback.
As a leader, you are only going to be as good as the people on your team. Be clear in your mind what good looks like, and don't compromise.

The results are remarkably consistent and reveal three key dimensions of great teamwork. The first is alignment on direction, where there is a shared belief about what the company is striving toward and the role of the team in getting there.
Teams have their own level of intelligence, which is separate from the combined intelligence of their team members." - from Building Great Teams
